explanation: Silas Crane was not stabbed, and he was not killed during the magic show. He was poisoned an hour before he died, by the man who had brought him the same drink every night for twenty-five years: Bingo the Clown.

Twenty years ago Bingo's wife, Lottie, fell from the trapeze on a frayed rope. Bingo had asked Silas three times to replace it. Tonight, clearing Silas's desk as he filled the siphon, Bingo found the old repair estimate in the back of the ledger: 'New trapeze rope, fourteen dollars. DECLINED. S.C.' Fourteen dollars.

At eleven o'clock Bingo filled the seltzer siphon as always, and stirred in a tin of Rough-on-Rats from the cookhouse shelf. Arsenic has almost no taste in fizzy water with ulcer powder. Horace, at a quarter past eleven, noticed the siphon smelled faintly of garlic and thought it was Silas's dinner.

Silas left the ring at 11:35 and, as every night, mixed his ulcer powder with seltzer at his desk. By half past twelve he was dead. Bingo's white clown greasepaint was on the siphon's nozzle, and the empty tin was in his trunk of spare noses.
The magician had the trick, the bearded lady had the threat, and the bookkeeper had the missing pages. The clown had twenty years, and fourteen dollars.

timeline.event: In the cookhouse, Silas announces the sale. Bertha threatens him. He tells Bingo there's no room for clowns.
A tin of Rough-on-Rats goes missing from the cookhouse shelf.
Bingo fills the seltzer siphon in the red wagon, finds the old rope estimate, and poisons the siphon.
Horace slips into the red wagon to tear pages from the ledger. The siphon smells of garlic.
Silas goes to his wagon and drinks his seltzer and ulcer powder.
The Vanishing Cabinet act. Mysterio spends it under the stage, as always.
Bertha knocks on the red wagon's door. No answer.
Samson finds Silas dead at his desk.

private.backstory: YOU ARE THE MURDERER. Twenty years ago your wife, Lottie, fell from the trapeze on a frayed rope you'd begged Silas three times to replace. Tonight at eleven, filling his seltzer siphon as you have every night for twenty-five years, you found the old repair estimate in the back of his ledger: 'New trapeze rope, fourteen dollars. DECLINED. S.C.' Fourteen dollars. You fetched the tin of Rough-on-Rats from the cookhouse shelf, stirred it into the siphon, and went on with your act. He drank it after he left the ring. You hid the empty tin in your trunk of spare noses.
objectives: Don't get caught. You fill that siphon every night; that's your cover, and your danger.
Point suspicion at Mysterio (his impossible alibi, his empty dagger slot) and at Bertha (her threat).
Get rid of that tin before anyone looks in your trunk.
knows: Rough-on-Rats is arsenic. It tastes of almost nothing in fizzy water, but it smells faintly of garlic.
Mysterio's cabinet trick has a trapdoor. Everyone in the ring crew half-knows it.

act3: I fill his seltzer every night. If I wanted to poison him, I'd have done it twenty years ago. Wouldn't I?

private.backstory: For twelve years your Vanishing Cabinet has sold Silas Crane's tickets. Last month Silas sold its secret, the trapdoor and the mirrors, to Barlow Brothers for two thousand dollars, and tonight he told you you're finished after Sunday. You could have killed him. You didn't. During the trick you did what you always do: dropped through the trapdoor and crouched in the dust under the stage for ten minutes, breathing sawdust, until it was time to reappear. Your real dagger isn't in its case because you pawned it in Dayton last month to pay the rent. You'd rather die than admit either of those things.
objectives: Protect the secret of the cabinet. The trapdoor is your whole career.
Don't let anyone learn you pawned the real dagger.
Find out who really killed Silas, before your 'impossible' alibi starts looking suspicious.
knows: Silas always drinks a glass of seltzer with his ulcer powder after the show. Bingo fills the siphon.
At dinner, Bertha told Silas: 'Sell me like a pig at a fair and see what happens.'
private.alibi: From 11:40 to 11:52 I was in the Vanishing Cabinet. Well. Under it. The details are a professional secret.

act3: I did not kill Silas Crane. Look at who handed him something to drink every single night. Look at who knew his habits.

knows: Your father left the ring at 11:35 to wire Barlow's. He handed you the top hat and said, 'Try not to ruin it.'
When the Vanishing Cabinet opened at 11:52, Mysterio's shoes were grey with sawdust and he was coughing. He always is, after that trick.
This morning you drew the Death card for Silas, and left it on his desk as a warning.
At a quarter to eleven you saw Bingo coming out of the cookhouse with something small and square under his coat, walking fast toward the red wagon.
At a quarter past eleven the stove in the red wagon was lit, and the seltzer siphon was on the desk, full. It smelled faintly of garlic, which you put down to Silas's dinner.
Silas wrote a riddle on the cover of his ledger to remind himself of the lock's combination, because he could never remember it.

prop-case.text: Mysterio's prop case, open in the backstage wagon, has two velvet slots for daggers. One holds the rubber trick dagger. The other, for the real steel blade, is empty, and has been dusty for weeks.

cabinet.text: Your own memory of the act: at 11:43, when you spun the locked cabinet, it moved like an empty crate, as it always does at that moment. You've kept the secret for years: during the trick, Mysterio is under the stage.

trapdoor.text: Under the centre-ring stage, the trapdoor beneath the Vanishing Cabinet is scuffed with boot prints. They go down into the dusty crawlspace under the stage, round in a small circle, and back up. They don't go anywhere near the canvas flap.

handkerchief.text: Tucked in the lining of Mysterio's cape: his red silk handkerchief, stained red. It's sticky and smells sweet: corn syrup and dye. Stage blood, for the act.

reading.text: Your own memory: this morning, while you read Silas's palm in the red wagon, Mysterio burst in, white with rage. 'You sold my cabinet, Silas. You'll pay for that.' Then he sat down and wept. You've never seen him cry.

siphon.text: On Silas's desk, beside his hand: his seltzer siphon and a glass with a white film of ulcer powder in the bottom. The siphon's water smells faintly, but unmistakably, of garlic. Bingo the clown fills that siphon for him every night.

puzzle.solvedText: Tucked into the back, a yellowed slip, much handled: 'Estimate: new trapeze rope, $14. DECLINED. S.C.' Beneath it, in Silas's hand, dated twenty years ago: 'Pike's wife fell today. Rope. If he ever sees this estimate, God help me.' Someone has smoothed it flat very recently.

addClues.title: The Missing Tin
addClues.text: The cookhouse cook reports a tin of Rough-on-Rats, arsenic rat poison, missing from the shelf since a quarter to eleven. An empty tin of that brand turns up in clown alley, stuffed in a trunk of spare red noses.

addClues.title: Clown White
addClues.text: On the siphon's nozzle and the wagon's door handle: smears of thick white greasepaint. Only one performer at Crane's wears a white face.

cues.text: Inside the red wagon: a desk, a ledger, a seltzer siphon, a coal stove, and a tarot card face up.

The doctor finds no wound and no bruise. The ringmaster's lips are tinged blue, and there's a sour smell of garlic on his breath. Arsenic, the doctor says, or I'm a Dutchman. Somebody gave Silas Crane something to drink.

cues.speaker: samson
cues.text: I found him at one. His hand was still on the ledger.

finale.text: Dawn over the fairground. A sheriff's car bumps across the muddy lot.
One last toast: to the detectives, and to Crane's Carnival of Wonders!
finale.alternative: Coffee cups up for the detectives!

finale.text: The sheriff arrived at six. Bingo the Clown was waiting on the steps of clown alley, face scrubbed clean for the first time in twenty-five years. 'Fourteen dollars,' he said, and held out his wrists.
As for the rest of the troupe: the sale is off, the will is read, and a magician, a lion and a bearded lady have some decisions to make. The show goes on. Goodnight, detectives.
